draft.title: Effects of colonisation on First Nations Australians
card: First Nations peoples had lived on and cared for their Country for tens of thousands of years. As British settlement spread from 1788, it changed life for communities in many harmful ways.
Disease
Settlers brought illnesses such as smallpox. First Nations people had no earlier exposure to these diseases, so they had little immunity, and many people died.
Loss of land
Settlers took land and cut off access to waterholes and rivers. Farms and livestock also reduced the plants and animals that people relied on for food.
Violence
Settlers, police and others used violence against communities who stayed on or defended their Country. Many people were killed.
draft.remember: Disease, lost land, water and food, and violence together devastated First Nations communities.

a.q: Why did smallpox cause so many deaths in First Nations communities?
opts: People had no earlier exposure, so had little immunity
People refused to accept any care from the settlers
The disease only spread when settlers attacked people
People had moved away from their rivers and waterholes
a.why: Smallpox was new to Australia, so people had little immunity and it spread quickly. Violence and lost land added to the harm, but the card does not say the disease depended on attacks.
a.clue: Think about whether the illness had been met before.

b.q: Settlers fenced off a river and ran sheep on the land beside it. A nearby community could no longer reach its waterholes or gather its usual foods. Which effect of colonisation does this best show?
opts: Loss of land, water and food sources
Death from a disease with no immunity
Violence used against people on their Country
A treaty made over the use of the land
b.why: Fencing off water and replacing native food sources with livestock removed what the community relied on. No disease or attack is described, so those are not the best fit. The card also notes that no treaty was made.
b.clue: Look at what the community could no longer reach or gather.

a.best: People had no earlier exposure, so had little immunity

b.best: Loss of land, water and food sources

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'The card also notes that no treaty was made', but this card says nothing about treaties. Treaties belong to point 2 (terra nullius), so the why misstates what the card teaches.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card. The only problem is that Why (b) wrongly claims the card mentions that no treaty was made. The 'settlers brought smallpox' framing is the standard school account, though historians still debate where the 1789 outbreak came from.
